name: ISPMT
description: ISPMT returns the interest paid in a given period, assuming the principal is repaid in equal installments rather than equal payments.
tldr: Calculates the interest paid during a specific period of a loan with equal principal payments.

parameters.name: per
parameters.description: The period for which to calculate interest.

basicExample.description: Interest for a specific period of an interest-only or equal-principal loan
basicExample.explanation: For a $12,000 loan at 5% annual interest, the first month's interest is $50 if principal is repaid equally.

advancedExamples.title: Later period interest
advancedExamples.description: Interest decreases as principal is repaid
advancedExamples.explanation: Because the principal balance declines, the interest also declines each period.

howItWorks: ISPMT calculates interest based on the outstanding principal balance at the start of the period. Unlike IPMT, it assumes equal principal payments rather than equal total payments.

howToSteps.name: Calculate
howToSteps.text: Press Enter to get the result.

limitations: ISPMT is different from IPMT. IPMT is for loans with equal payments.

commonErrors.fix: Use IPMT for standard amortized loans with equal payments.

commonErrors.cause: Per is outside the range 1 to nper.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: ISPMT works identically in Google Sheets.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Same syntax and behavior as Excel.

faq.question: What is the difference between ISPMT and IPMT?
faq.answer: ISPMT assumes equal principal payments. IPMT assumes equal total payments.

faq.question: When should I use ISPMT?
faq.answer: Use it for loans where the principal is repaid in equal installments, not typical amortized loans.
